notes: The uniqueness half is settled and holds (the refuter's d01, d05, d07, d08, d09). The FILLER half: 'this series' has two candidate antecedents, the enumeration in SR6's first sentence and the 'series of data-names' that GR2 names as the second option. The text decides for the second option: (1) GR2 is where the standard itself calls an option of this entry a 'series', and FILLER is needed only there, because the series is positional ('taken in order, correspond to') and a member cannot be left out, whereas a clause that defines no name is simply omitted (the 87- or 33-position record is allocated either way, GR2; SR4 'neither option'); (2) the contrast inside the same entry: Format 2, which has clauses and no series option, prints the uniqueness sentence (SR10) WITHOUT the FILLER sentence, so FILLER is granted exactly where a series option exists and nowhere a clause stands alone. Under the enumeration reading Format 2's clauses would deserve the same grant and do not get it. So SYMBOLIC QUEUE IS FILLER and MESSAGE DATE IS FILLER are not language the 1985 text provides, and COBOL6169 is right; FILLER in the series is accepted and runs. Precedence check: GnuCOBOL 3.2 (cobc/parser.y named_input_cd_clause and unnamed_input_cd_clauses take 'identifier' only) admits FILLER in neither option, so it does not contradict the reading. Cosmetic, not a conformance defect: the FILLER diagnostic quotes 'ISO/IEC 1989:2002 A.1.2.2' at --std 85 (the same words are §1985:XIV.2.2.3 SR6/SR15); the file's other CD diagnostics cite 2002 the same way. Implementor choice: Does 'Within this series' (SR6, SR15) let FILLER replace the data-name of a clause of the first option? Decided by the text (GR2's 'series of data-names' is the second option; Format 2's SR10 omits the FILLER grant where no series option exists); GnuCOBOL 3.2 admits FILLER in neither option, so precedence yields no contrary practice; documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.3, row "FILLER in a CD entry".
